planning_scheme.name: Redland City Plan 2018 (cited as the 'Redland planning scheme')
planning_scheme.version: Version 14 (Major amendment; PDF consolidation 'updated 23 September 2026 with changes to SC 5')
planning_scheme.notes: Scheme commenced 8 October 2018 (Citation and commencement). Appendix 2 Table AP2.1: version 14 'Adopted 17 September 2025 ... Effective 10 November 2025', Major amendment (MDR, LMDR and TA zone codes; ROL code; tables of assessment for LMDR/MDR; PSP 7). The council-hosted PDF is labelled 'updated 23 September 2026 with changes to SC 5' (Schedule 5 change; version number unchanged). Pending: Major Amendment 02/25 - Residential (and 03/25 Non-residential): council resolved 15 July 2026 to seek Planning Minister approval to adopt; NOT in force as at 8 Oct 2026. There are no local plans in the scheme; precincts within zone codes do the localisation. A new 'Redlands Coast City Plan (RCCP)' is in preparation (council page link).

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: City Plan v14 refers only to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2/MP1.3; it has NOT been amended to refer to the Queensland Housing Code (no 'Housing Code'/'QHC' text in v14 or in the 02/25 consultation draft). Section 1.6 names the LDR zone code (plus bushfire, coastal, flood, heritage overlay codes and Tables 5.6.1/5.9.1) as containing building assessment provisions. Only Low density residential zone precinct provisions (LDR2, LDR4, LDR1/LDR2 site cover, LDR5 canal setback, LDR3 site cover/component size/height) are expressly alternative provisions. Other LDR precinct AOs are expressly NOT alternative provisions and instead trigger code-assessable 'Building Work Assessable Against the Planning Scheme'. Everywhere else QDC (now QHC) siting applies unmodified. How the QDC references map to the QHC after 1 Sept 2026 is a transitional/interpretation question for the Building Act - not addressed in the scheme.

definitions.text: Note--As prescribed by section 8(1) of the Planning Regulation the administrative terms and their definitions are located in schedule 4 columns 1 and 2 of the Regulation.

setback, for a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.
definitions.clause: Planning Regulation 2017 sch 4 (current as at 11 Sept 2026), adopted via SC1.2

definitions.text: site cover, of development, means the portion of the site, expressed as a percentage, that will be covered by a building or structure, measured to its outermost projection, after the development is carried out, other than a building or structure, or part of a building or structure, that is-- (a) in a landscaped or open space area, including, for example, a gazebo or shade structure; or (b) a basement that is completely below ground level and used for car parking; or (c) the eaves of a building; or (d) a sun shade.

building height, of a building, means-- (a) the vertical distance, measured in metres, between the ground level of the building and the highest point on the roof of the building, other than a point that is part of an aerial, chimney, flagpole or load-bearing antenna; or (b) the number of storeys in the building above ground level.

outermost projection, of a building or structure, means the outermost part of the building or structure, other than a part that is-- (a) a retractable blind; or (b) a fixed screen; or (c) a rainwater fitting; or (d) an ornamental attachment.
site, of development, means the land that the development is to be carried out on.
ground level means-- (a) the level of the natural ground; or (b) if the level of the natural ground has changed, the level as lawfully changed.

storey-- (a) means a space within a building between 2 floor levels, or a floor level and a ceiling or roof, other than-- (i) a space containing only a lift shaft, stairway or meter room; or (ii) a space containing only a bathroom, shower room, laundry, toilet or other sanitary compartment; or (iii) a space containing only a combination of the things stated in subparagraph (i) or (ii); or (iv) a basement with a ceiling that is not more than 1m above ground level; and (b) includes-- (i) a mezzanine; and (ii) a roofed structured that is on, or part of, a rooftop, if the structure does not only accommodate building plant and equipment.
domestic outbuilding means a non-habitable class 10a building that is-- (a) a shed, garage or carport; and (b) ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.

dwelling house means a residential use of premises involving-- (a) 1 dwelling and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or (b) 2 dwellings, 1 of which is a secondary dwelling, and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.
definitions.clause: Planning Regulation 2017 sch 24 (sch 3 cross-refers); adopted by SC1.1

definitions.text: The two-dimensional extent of built development, including balconies, covered private outdoor living areas and enclosed spaces but excluding the part of a building or structure that is: - an eave or a roof; or - a sunhood or the like attached to the wall of a building or structure to provide shade or shelter to the wall.
A lot which has access to a road by means only of an access strip which forms part of the lot, or by means only of an easement over adjoining land.

rules.verbatim_text: PO13 The height of a building does not unduly: (1) overshadow adjoining houses; and (2) obstruct the outlook from adjoining lots. AO13.1 For slopes up to 15%, building height is 8.5m, except for roofs or pergolas covering decks. These may extend to 10m above ground level, providing: (1) they cover an area of no more than 10m2; (2) there is only one such covered areas on each detached building component on the site; and (3) the covered area is not enclosed by walls. Editor's note--This provision establishes an alternative solution to the Queensland Development Code for buildings on slopes <15%. For buildings on slopes >15%, the acceptable solution under the Queensland Development Code applies.

exceptions: roofs or pergolas covering decks may extend to 10m above ground level if <=10m2, only one per detached building component, not enclosed by walls

local_plan_mechanism.summary: City Plan v14 has NO local plans ('5.8 ... There are no local plans in the planning scheme.'). Localised variation is achieved through zone precincts in the Low density residential zone code (LDR1 large lot, LDR2 park residential, LDR3 Point Lookout residential, LDR4 Kinross Road, LDR5 Canal and Lakeside Estates). Precinct membership is mapped in Figures 6.2.1.2.1-6.2.1.2.5 and on zone maps. Precinct status changes the level of assessment (Table 5.4.1/5.6.1) and brings in precinct-specific AOs, some of which are QDC alternative provisions.

examples.quote: AO4.1 In precinct LDR2 park residential, dwelling houses (including outbuildings) are set back 10m from a road frontage and 10m from a side or rear boundary.

examples.plan: Precinct LDR5 Canal and Lakeside Estates
examples.quote: AO9.1 Development (including domestic outbuildings and other roofed structures, but excluding in-ground swimming pools) is setback a minimum of 9m from the property boundary adjoining a canal or lake.

open_questions: QHC transition: City Plan v14 alternative provisions reference the QDC (MP1.1/MP1.2) only. Whether/how they continue to operate as alternative provisions against the QHC (QDC Parts 1.1/1.2 from 1 Sept 2026) depends on Building Act/Regulation transitional provisions - not addressed in the scheme; needs state-level confirmation.
Precinct mapping: rules depend on precinct boundaries (LDR1-LDR5) - need GIS layer (council zoning/precinct mapping) to apply.

LDR5 AO9.1: whether unroofed decks, above-ground pools and pool equipment are 'development' caught by the 9m canal setback - text says 'including domestic outbuildings and other roofed structures, but excluding in-ground swimming pools'.
LDR3 AO12.1 'size' of a building component - GFA or footprint undefined.
LDR1/LDR2 AO6.1: heading note says 'A number of the following' AOs are alternative provisions; only AO6.1 follows - treated as alternative provision.
Conservation zone: dwelling house not listed in Table 5.4.15 (inferred impact assessable) - confirm.

Pending Major Amendment 02/25 - Residential (council resolved 15 July 2026 to request Ministerial approval): would make dwelling houses in the character residential zone accepted subject to requirements with a road-setback performance outcome as an alternative provision, add swimming pools/excavation to LDR5 triggers, change LDR3 AO16.1 for domestic outbuildings, and change LDR corner-lot/dual occupancy rules. Re-check after adoption.
